videos.title: Where Does Light Get Its Speed From?
videos.description:
🎧 Hi! We're now on Spotify! Listen to us anytime, anywhere: https://open.spotify.com/show/034375jF5GNTY1FMcUihE7 

Light travels at 299,792.458 kilometers per second. 

That number is so fundamental that physicists use it to define the meter itself. But almost nobody knows where it comes from, what gives it that speed, and why the universe couldn't have made it any other way.

The answer connects empty space, quantum mechanics, the geometry of spacetime, and the reason atoms can exist at all. Change that number even slightly and chemistry breaks down, stars burn out in an instant, and life becomes impossible anywhere in the universe.
One of the deepest constants in all of physics. And it runs deeper than most people ever realize.

tags: science facts to fall asleep to

videos.title: Why Light Never Ages... And What That Really Means for Physics
tags: does time stop at the speed of light
what happens at the speed of light
videos.description:
Light doesn't age.

A photon can cross billions of light-years of space and arrive having experienced zero time. Zero. That single fact quietly breaks everything you thought you knew about how the universe works.

Space and time are not fixed. They bend, stretch, and run at different rates. The faster you move, the slower you age. Clocks on satellites tick differently than clocks on the ground, and your phone corrects for that every time you ask it for directions.

But the deeper you follow this idea, the stranger it gets. What does it mean that the fastest thing in existence experiences none of the journey? What does that tell us about the nature of time itself, about what light actually is, and about how we came to know any of this at all?

where does an electron get its energy

videos.title: Why Do Particles Have Spin If Nothing Is Actually Spinning?
tags: what is spin in quantum mechanics
videos.description:
Every particle in the universe carries a property called spin. Electrons have it, protons have it, photons have it. It shapes the structure of atoms, determines why matter is solid, and is responsible for chemistry, magnetism, and the existence of stars. Without it, nothing complex could exist.

The strange part? None of those particles are actually spinning.

Spin is one of the most precisely measured quantities in all of science, confirmed to ten decimal places, and built into the deepest equations physics has ever produced. Yet it has no axis, no rotation, and no equivalent anywhere in the everyday world. The name itself is a historical accident that stuck around long after everyone realized it was wrong.

What it actually is runs far deeper than the word suggests.

videos.title: Inside a Neutron Star... Matter Stops Existing as We Know It
tags: what is a neutron star made of
videos.description:
Have you ever tried to imagine what happens to matter when it's pushed past every limit physics allows? Inside a neutron star, matter is compressed into a state that has no equivalent anywhere else in the observable universe. A single teaspoon of this material would outweigh every aircraft carrier ever built, combined, many times over. Gravity here is so extreme that light itself bends around the surface. Deep inside, protons and electrons are crushed together until they stop existing as we know them, and matter reorganizes itself into something physicists are still working to fully understand. Neutron stars are the densest objects that can exist without collapsing completely, and what's happening inside them is one of the biggest open questions in modern physics.

videos.title: What Is a Photon Actually Made Of… And Why Does It Never Stand Still?
tags: why does light never slow down
videos.description:
A photon has no mass, no size, and no experience of time. It carries the energy that powers every star, the force that holds every atom together, and every image your eyes have ever formed.

And yet the question of what one actually is took three centuries and several complete revolutions in physics to even partially answer.

It behaves like a particle in one experiment and like a wave in another, and both results are correct. It has momentum but no mass. It experiences no time between the moment it is created and the moment it is absorbed. And it cannot, under any circumstances, ever slow down.

What a photon actually is at the deepest level is one of the strangest answers in all of science.

videos.title: What Is a Wormhole... Really?
videos.description:
What if the fabric of space could fold, and two points billions of light years apart could be connected by a tunnel shorter than a room? 

The idea sounds like science fiction, but wormholes are a direct consequence of Einstein's equations, sitting inside the mathematics of general relativity since nineteen sixteen. Physicists have spent decades trying to understand what they actually are, whether they can exist, and why every attempt to make one stable keeps running into the same wall. The answers involve black holes, quantum entanglement, negative energy, and some of the deepest unsolved problems in physics. General relativity actually allows this, and the deeper you go, the stranger it gets.
